title: The call of the fishermen and the great catch

en.4:18: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
en.4:19: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”
en.4:20: And at once they left their nets and followed Him.
en.4:21: Going on from there, He saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets. Jesus called them,
en.4:22: and immediately they left the boat and their father and followed Him.

en.1:16: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
en.1:17: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”
en.1:18: And at once they left their nets and followed Him.
en.1:19: Going on a little farther, He saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat, mending their nets.
en.1:20: Immediately Jesus called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and followed Him.

en.5:1: On one occasion, while Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret with the crowd pressing in on Him to hear the word of God,
en.5:2: He saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.
en.5:3: Jesus got into the boat belonging to Simon and asked him to put out a little from shore. And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.
en.5:4: When Jesus had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”
en.5:5: “Master,” Simon replied, “we have worked hard all night without catching anything. But because You say so, I will let down the nets.”
en.5:6: When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.
en.5:7: So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
en.5:8: When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees. “Go away from me, Lord,” he said, “for I am a sinful man.”
en.5:9: For he and his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken,
en.5:10: and so were his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee. “Do not be afraid,” Jesus said to Simon. “From now on you will catch men.”
en.5:11: And when they had brought their boats ashore, they left everything and followed Him.

en.21:1: Later, by the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus again revealed Himself to the disciples. He made Himself known in this way:
en.21:2: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples were together.
en.21:3: Simon Peter told them, “I am going fishing.” “We will go with you,” they said. So they went out and got into the boat, but caught nothing that night.
en.21:4: Early in the morning, Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples did not recognize that it was Jesus.
en.21:5: So He called out to them, “Children, do you have any fish?” “No,” they answered.
en.21:6: He told them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” So they cast it there, and they were unable to haul it in because of the great number of fish.
en.21:7: Then the disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!” As soon as Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on his outer garment (for he had removed it) and jumped into the sea.
en.21:8: The other disciples came ashore in the boat. They dragged in the net full of fish, for they were not far from land, only about a hundred yards.
en.21:9: When they landed, they saw a charcoal fire there with fish on it, and some bread.
en.21:10: Jesus told them, “Bring some of the fish you have just caught.”
en.21:11: So Simon Peter went aboard and dragged the net ashore. It was full of large fish, 153, but even with so many, the net was not torn.
en.21:12: “Come, have breakfast,” Jesus said to them. None of the disciples dared to ask Him, “Who are You?” They knew it was the Lord.
en.21:13: Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and He did the same with the fish.
en.21:14: This was now the third time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after He was raised from the dead.

mt-mk.runText: Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ
